newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Analysts see Ciba SC prices up to 100 Sfr.
newsitem.headline: Analysts see Ciba SC prices up to 100 Sfr.

text.p: Swiss analysts said they expected shares in Ciba Specialty Chemicals Holdings Inc to trade around 100 Swiss francs each as the company is spun off from Novartis AG.

"A lot of potential would be taken out in advance with a price of 100 francs," said Beat Kaeser at Societe Generale Bank & Trust (SGBT), adding Ciba must still prove that restructuring measures will have a quick positive effect on operating margins.

Strong retail demand pushed grey market quotes for Ciba shares to around 109 to 111 francs, dealers said, but they noted the thin market was keeping prices rather high above the indicated public offer price of 72 to 86 Swiss francs per share.

The indicative price range announced last week values the company at up to 6.21 billion francs. The final issue price and allotment will be announced on March 13 after a complicated system of book-building is completed.

Rights for the shares start trading tomorrow and should be around 10 francs below the expected share price, given the 10 franc exercise price for Novartis shareholders getting them in a one-for-one rights issue.

Lead organisers Credit Suisse First Boston and Union Bank of Switzerland are expected to announce around 1800 GMT today the minimum "floor" price at which a bank consortium will offer to buy the rights.
The consortium will use the rights to get Ciba shares that will be offered to the public in a global issue of at least 300 million francs worth of shares. Share trading starts March 13.
Zurich Cantonal Bank estimated the shares would trade for 90 to 95 francs, one banker there said, adding prices above 100 were too high.
Bankers declined to rule out erratic price movements once rights trading starts, adding some investors who bought Novartis shares solely for the rights to Ciba SC might take profits.
"A lot of shaky hands will take part in the issue to make a quick profit," said one banker who asked not to be named.
Kaeser said he thought prices would come off in the first few days of trading.

He said it was important to see how shares of Novartis react to the loss of its rights to Ciba. He estimated Novartis stock would weaken but not by the full value of the rights, but analysts disagreed on this point.
